questions.stem: £4000 is put into a savings account paying 4% compound interest a year. How much is in the account after 2 years? Give your answer to the nearest penny.
worked: Compound interest: each year's interest is added, so the next year's is worked out on the new amount. The multiplier is 100% + 4% = 104% = 1.04.
As a power: 4000 × 1.04^2 = 4326.4, which is £4326.40 to the nearest penny.

slip.line: That is simple interest: the same amount every year. Compound interest is worked out on the new amount each year, so use the multiplier 1.04 once for each year.
The multiplier was multiplied by the number of years. It has to be applied once for each year: 4000 × 1.04^2.
A 4% rise has the multiplier 1.04, not 1.4.
